34.commentaire: This verse teaches us that each generation has its role to play in God's plan. No matter our past or struggles, God can use us for His glory. As Christians, we must remember that our identity is in Christ, and that, like Michée, we are called to reflect God's greatness in our lives.

mots.sens: The name Michée (מִיכָאֵל) means 'Who is like God?'. This name evokes an affirmation of God's greatness and sovereignty, emphasizing the idea that no one can compare to Him. In the context of this verse, it represents a lineage that is connected to the divine promise, reminding us that each descendant has a role in God's plan.

The name Pithon (פִּיתוֹן) may be derived from the Hebrew word meaning 'to open' or 'to liberate'. This term can symbolize an opening to new opportunities or liberation from constraints. Spiritually, it can be interpreted as a promise of deliverance and new possibilities for the descendants of Michée.

The word Mélec (מֶלֶךְ) means 'king'. This term refers to authority, sovereignty, and governance. In a spiritual context, it reminds us that God is the supreme King and that each descendant has a responsibility to live under His lordship, thereby reflecting His character in the world.

Achaz (אֲחָז) means 'he has seized' or 'he has taken'. This name can symbolize a taking of possession or an appropriation of God's promises. In the context of this verse, it underscores the importance of seizing the blessings and responsibilities that God grants to each generation.

35.epoque: This passage is set in the context of the post-exilic period, when the people of Israel were seeking to rebuild their identity and lineage after returning from Babylon.
35.passage: 1 Chronicles 8 is part of a genealogy that traces the descendants of Benjamin, highlighting the importance of lineages in Israel's history and their role in God's plan.
35.culture: In Israelite culture, genealogies were crucial for establishing identity, rights of inheritance, and social status. They testify to God's faithfulness to His promises to His people.
35.interpretation: This verse, although it seems to contain names, reminds us that each individual has a place in the divine plan. The descendants of Michée carry within them the spiritual heritage and responsibility to live according to God's ways.
35.commentaire: The study of this verse encourages us to recognize the importance of our spiritual roots and heritage. Each name mentioned here represents a story and a call to live for God's glory. As believers, we are called to seize our identity in Christ and to pass this faith on to future generations.

mots.sens: Achaz means 'he has seized' or 'he has taken'. This name evokes a notion of taking power or control, which is relevant in the context of the kings of Judah. Spiritually, it can symbolize the way God allows some to reign according to His purposes, even if their actions are not always in line with His will.

Jehoadda means 'Yahweh has known'. This name emphasizes the personal relationship between God and the individual, indicating that God is aware and attentive to those who belong to Him. In the context of genealogy, it reminds us that each generation is known and carried by God in His redemptive plan.

Zimri means 'song' or 'to praise'. This word evokes the idea of praise and celebration, which is significant within the lineage of David. Spiritually, it reminds us that even within human lineages, there is a call to glorify God through our lives and our legacies.

Motsa means 'exit' or 'outcome'. This term can be interpreted as a reference to the paths that God opens for His people. In the context of genealogy, it underscores that each generation has a role to play in the divine plan, and that God guides each 'exit' toward a specific purpose.

36.epoque: This passage is set in the context of the Old Testament, during the period of the kings of Judah, where lineages and genealogies were essential for establishing the heritage and legitimacy of leaders.
36.passage: 1 Chronicles 8 primarily deals with the lineages of Benjamin and highlights the importance of descent in God's plan for Israel. This particular verse sheds light on the continuity of the lineage through specific generations.
36.culture: In Israelite culture, genealogy was crucial for establishing tribal identity and the right to the promised land. Each name in the genealogy carried meaning and a story, reinforcing the idea of the covenant between God and His people.
36.interpretation: This passage illustrates God's faithfulness through the generations, showing how He has orchestrated the history of His people. Each name mentioned represents not only a person but also a spiritual heritage and a promise of God to Israel.
36.commentaire: The genealogy of 1 Chronicles 8:36 reminds us that God works through generations, and that each life has a purpose in His plan. As believers, we are called to recognize our spiritual heritage and to live in a way that honors God, while passing our faith on to future generations.

mots.sens: The word 'Motsa' means 'exit' or 'escape'. It is derived from the Hebrew root that evokes the idea of leaving a place or situation. In the context of genealogy, this can symbolize a new beginning or continuity in the lineage, highlighting the importance of each generation in God's divine plan.

The name 'Binea' is composed of the root 'bana', which means 'to build'. This evokes the idea of building not only physical structures but also relationships and spiritual legacies. In this verse, Binea represents a generation that contributes to the building of God's people.

The word 'Rapha' means 'to heal' or 'to restore'. This can refer to a spiritual dimension where God restores His people. In the mentioned lineage, this can symbolize the hope of healing and redemption for future generations.

The name 'Éleasa' means 'God has helped'. This word emphasizes divine intervention in the lives of individuals and families. In the context of this passage, it reminds us that each generation is the fruit of God's grace and providence.

37.epoque: This passage is set in a post-exilic period, where the people of Israel seek to regain their identity and lineage after years of dispersion.
37.passage: In 1 Chronicles 8, the author focuses on the genealogy of the tribe of Benjamin, highlighting the importance of ancestors and their descendants in God's plan.
37.culture: Genealogy holds great significance in Hebrew culture, as it establishes links of kinship and identity within God's people, reinforcing the sense of community and heritage.
37.interpretation: This verse, although it seems to be a simple list of names, emphasizes the continuity of God's promise through the generations. Each name represents a story, a contribution, and a legacy that is passed down from father to son.
37.commentaire: This passage reminds us that each generation has a role to play in God's plan. As believers, we are called to build on the legacy of those who have gone before us, while passing on our faith and values to future generations. Let us reflect on the impact we have on our family and community, committing ourselves to be builders in God's kingdom.

mots.sens: The name Atsel means 'one who is near' or 'the neighbor'. It evokes a notion of closeness and relationship, which can be interpreted as an invitation to communion and unity within the family of Israel. In the context of genealogy, this underscores the importance of family ties among God's people.

The term 'בָּנִים' means 'sons' and refers to descendants and the continuity of the lineage. In Hebrew culture, sons are often seen as heirs and bearers of family and spiritual identity. This highlights the importance of passing on God's values and promises through the generations.

The word 'שֵׁם' means 'name' and holds great significance in Hebrew culture, as the name is often associated with a person's identity and character. In this verse, the names of Atsel's sons can be seen as testimonies of their heritage and their role in the history of God's people, thus emphasizing the importance of knowing and honoring our ancestors.

38.epoque: This passage is set in the historical context of the return of the Babylonian exiles and the rebuilding of the Jewish community in Jerusalem, after the period of captivity.
38.passage: 1 Chronicles 8 focuses on the genealogy of the descendants of Benjamin, highlighting the importance of lineages and families in the history of Israel. This verse specifies the names of Atsel's sons, emphasizing their place in this lineage.
38.culture: In Hebrew culture, genealogy is essential for understanding a person's identity and status within the community. Names often carry deep meanings and are chosen to reflect character traits or significant events.
38.interpretation: This verse reminds us that every individual, even those who seem less known, has a place and a role in God's plan. The names of Atsel's sons are a testimony to God's faithfulness through the generations and His commitment to His people.
38.commentaire: The study of this verse encourages us to recognize and value our spiritual and familial heritage. As believers, we are called to pass on our faith and values to future generations, just as Atsel passed his name to his sons. Let us reflect on how we can be models of faith and integrity for those around us.

mots.sens: This word designates a proper name, Eshékh, which means 'ink' or 'mark'. In the context of genealogy, it represents an important lineage in the history of Israel, underscoring the significance of descent and family relationships. Spiritually, this reminds us that each individual has a place in God's plan and that families play a crucial role in the transmission of faith.

Ulam is a name that can be interpreted as 'a young man' or 'a hero'. He is mentioned as the firstborn of Eshékh, which gives him a position of responsibility and honor in the lineage. Theologically, this underscores the importance of primogeniture in Israelite culture and how God chooses leaders from among families.

This name, which means 'salvation', is borne by the second son, Jeusch. It evokes the idea of deliverance and divine protection. In the spiritual context, this reminds us that salvation is a central theme of the Christian faith and that each generation must turn to God for its redemption.

Éliphelet, the third son, means 'God has delivered'. This name emphasizes God's faithfulness to deliver His people. Spiritually, this reminds us that God is always present to help us in our trials and that our trust in Him is essential.

39.epoque: This passage is set during the period of the kings of Israel, where genealogy and family heritage were crucial for the nation. It was a time when the tribes sought to establish their identity and place among God's people.
39.passage: 1 Chronicles 8 primarily deals with the genealogies of the descendants of Benjamin, highlighting the importance of lineage and heritage. This chapter reminds us that the history of Israel is founded on families and relationships.
39.culture: In Israelite culture, genealogy was essential for determining inheritance rights and social roles. Names often carried deep meanings, reflecting events or spiritual characteristics.
39.interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of family and descent in God's plan. Each name mentioned has a meaning that points to spiritual truths and God's faithfulness to His people.
39.commentaire: This passage reminds us that God is attentive to each generation and that He has a plan for every family. As believers, we must value our family relationships and pass on our faith to future generations, knowing that God works through our lineages to fulfill His promises.

mots.sens: The name 'Ulam' evokes a specific lineage within the tribe of Benjamin. It is associated with characteristics of strength and bravery, which is emphasized by the fact that his sons were 'valiant men.' The root of the word may suggest an idea of protection and defense, which is relevant in the military context of the time. Spiritually, this reminds us of the importance of strength and courage in our faith, as soldiers of Christ.

The term 'gibbor' means 'valiant' or 'hero,' and it is often used to designate warriors or men of valor in the Bible. This word emphasizes not only physical capability but also the moral and spiritual character of those who fight for justice and truth. In this verse, it highlights the legacy of bravery and strength that the descendants of Ulam have passed down, which is a call to be fighters of the faith.

The word 'hets' means 'arrow' or 'bow,' and it is symbolic of war and protection. In the biblical context, the bow is often associated with power and the ability to defend one's people. This reminds believers of the necessity to prepare spiritually for life's battles, using the weapons of faith to advance in the kingdom of God.

The name 'Benjamin' means 'son of the right hand,' symbolizing divine favor and strength. Benjamin is also known for his bravery and role in the history of Israel. In this verse, he represents a lineage of faithful warriors, which underscores the importance of spiritual heritage and values passed down from generation to generation.

40.epoque: This passage is set in a post-exilic period when the Israelites were seeking to establish their identity and heritage after returning from Babylon.
40.passage: In 1 Chronicles 8, the author focuses on the descendants of Benjamin, highlighting their history and significance in God's plan for Israel.
40.culture: The culture of the time valued bravery and military skill, and lineages were often celebrated for their contribution to the security and prosperity of the people.
40.interpretation: This verse emphasizes that even within families, there exists a legacy of strength and bravery that can be passed down. Spiritually, this reminds us that we are called to be warriors of the faith, ready to defend our convictions and pass on our spiritual heritage to future generations.
40.commentaire: The passage encourages us to recognize the importance of our spiritual heritage and to be 'valiant men' in our walk with God. As believers, we must prepare to face life's challenges with courage and determination, while passing on our faith to the next generations. May our lives be a testimony of strength and faithfulness, like that of the sons of Ulam.
